_rule: The lever register: one entry per handle on the methylation channel, the single source for the lever chapter and for DEV-LEVERS-01. Every entry names the term of the law it moves (foundation.json ids), its derivation and status, what it predicts with no free parameters, its caveat, its synthetic test with the bar written before running, the data it needs, and - required - its FALSIFIER: the reading that would break IAM here, written before any data is read. CANON/levers_check.py refuses an entry with no falsifier and refuses a lever in the chapter with no entry (and the reverse).

levers.name: Body temperature
levers.mechanism: kT appears twice: in the thermal quantum the drive is measured against (M = E_drive/kT) and in the holding energy E_hold = kT ln(g/f). A different operating temperature moves the floor directly.
levers.derivation: DERIVED: at fixed drive energy, M scales as 1/T, so eps_0 = 1/(1+e^{phi M}) rises with T with no free parameter once phi M is measured at 310 K.
levers.parameter_free: yes - the ratio of holding energies between two temperatures is set by the temperature ratio alone
levers.caveat: every temperature in a cross-species series is a different animal; thermal chemical damage rises with T as well, with an activation energy we do not know
levers.synthetic_outcome: run 2026-10-13: a cross-species series is weak (18 of 108 designs detect anything; 10 % damage share reachable only when species differ by at most 3 % for other reasons). Hibernation removes the species difference by construction.
levers.data: hibernator tissue at warm and cold body temperature, same animals; birds (40-42 C) as a second line; fish as a third
levers.falsifier: the same animal's cells at 5 C and at 37 C read the SAME holding energy within the measurement error, or move in the opposite direction to the temperature ratio. That breaks the floor's temperature dependence, which is IAM's law applied to the cell.
levers.reading_scope: The gauge reads order against disorder; the handle is the experiment, not the reading.
levers.falsifier_scope_why: kT sits in the floor and in the holding energy directly; a within-animal warm/cold reading needs no biology in between, so a null there is a failure of the law

levers.name: Division rate
levers.mechanism: division does not set the held error: the balance does. Division sets how fast the balance is reached, about 1/(f+g) intervals.
levers.derivation: DERIVED: eps = f/(f+g) is independent of the number of intervals once the balance is reached; the approach to it is geometric with rate (f+g).
levers.parameter_free: yes - cells that never divide must hold the same balance as dividing cells of the same type, and must not drift with age once at balance
levers.caveat: division rate travels with age, tissue and culture, so it cannot be varied on its own in human data
levers.synthetic_outcome: run 2026-10-13: about 20 donors detect a drift in the balance of 5-10 % across a lifetime; the reader's false-positive rate at no drift is 0.050.
levers.data: sorted neurons from two independent laboratories across an age span (DEV-IAMA-NEURON-01)
levers.falsifier: sorted neurons show the held error rising with age beyond 10 % across a lifetime while their restore and loss rates are unchanged. At balance it must not rise; a rise with unchanged rates contradicts the derivation.
levers.reading_scope: The gauge reads order against disorder; the handle is the experiment, not the reading.
levers.falsifier_scope_why: the balance says the held error is set by the ratio of restore to loss and NOT by the number of divisions; a non-dividing cell whose held error climbs with age contradicts the balance itself

levers.name: Methyl supply (SAM, methionine, folate, B12)
levers.mechanism: the restore rate g depends on the supply of methyl groups, so starving the supply lowers g and moves the balance towards more error.
levers.derivation: PARTLY DERIVED: the direction is derived (lower g raises eps = f/(f+g)); the size needs the dose-to-rate relation, which is measured, not derived.
levers.parameter_free: no - direction only, until the dose-to-rate relation is measured
levers.caveat: starvation also stops division, which only changes how fast the balance is reached, and starves much else besides methylation
levers.data: methionine restriction series (DEV-METHIONINE-01, parked); folate and B12 intervention arrays
levers.falsifier: restricting the methyl supply enough to lower the restore rate measurably leaves the held error unchanged, or lowers it. Either contradicts eps = f/(f+g).
levers.reading_scope: The gauge reads order against disorder; the handle is the experiment, not the reading.
levers.falsifier_scope_why: the dose-to-rate relation between supply and the restore rate is not derived; a null means our account of the medium is wrong, not that the law is

levers.name: Write and erase enzymes (DNMT, TET)
levers.mechanism: the write enzymes set g and the erasers set f, so impairing either moves the balance in a derived direction.
levers.derivation: DERIVED in direction and in ratio: halving g must move the balance to eps = f/(f+g/2), with no free parameter if g/f is read from the healthy balance first.
levers.parameter_free: yes - the new balance follows from the old one and the factor the enzyme was impaired by
levers.caveat: the drugs used to impair writing are toxic and stop division too; dose and exposure are rarely known in public data
levers.synthetic_outcome: test 3 designed (three channels: copy, de novo, erase), not yet run
levers.data: decitabine series (no result at the decisive dose); IDH-mutant tumors as an erase-channel block that already exists in patients with public data
levers.status: test 3 MET in simulation (2026-10-13): the erase channel is separated by direction alone - it is the only one that moves the held error down - and no pair overlaps in both readings at a matched impairment. Limit: copy and de novo separate only by the SIZE of the move, so with an unknown impairment magnitude they are not distinguishable by these two readings
levers.falsifier: a tumor whose erase channel is chemically blocked reads the SAME balance as a matched tumor with the channel intact, with everything else equal. If blocking one side of the balance does not move it, the balance is not what sets the held error.
levers.reading_scope: The gauge reads order against disorder; the handle is the experiment, not the reading.
levers.falsifier_scope_why: which operation an enzyme serves, and how far a chemical block reaches it, is biology in the way of the term
levers.next: IDH-mutant tumors, where the erase channel is chemically blocked in patients with public data; and the run-length spectrum as a third reading to separate copy from de novo by shape rather than size

levers.name: Clustered versus scattered failure
levers.mechanism: a processive enzyme that fails leaves runs of consecutive errors; independent chemical damage leaves isolated ones. The clustering reading separates them at matched total error.
levers.derivation: DERIVED: the variance of block means scales differently with run length for processive and independent failure.
levers.parameter_free: yes - the clustering reading is a ratio against the healthy baseline on the same platform
levers.caveat: only separates once a failure runs over about ten consecutive sites; below that the two are indistinguishable at array depth
levers.synthetic_outcome: run 2026-10-13, BAR MET: 35 of 36 conditions show no overlap across 200 draws; the failure is the weakest condition (runs of 5), which fixes the boundary.
levers.data: already in hand: every scored cancer cohort carries the clustering reading
levers.status: met in simulation; the boundary is stated
levers.falsifier: a cancer whose loss is known to be processive reads scattered, or a known chemical exposure reads clustered. That would mean the reading does not measure mechanism at all.
levers.reading_scope: The reading separates ISOLATED errors from errors that RUN TOGETHER. That is a property of the pattern, not of a machine. Calling a run-together pattern 'processive enzymatic failure' is an inference outside the physics and is labelled as such wherever stated.
levers.falsifier_scope_why: that a given failure runs along the strand is an assumption about the medium; what the law owns is only that isolated and run-together disorder are different patterns

chapter_opening:
The author's framing of what the gauge is, and the opening the lever chapter should keep (2026-10-13, his words):

Feeling the foreheads of fifty people with the back of your hand tells you who is hottest IN THAT ROOM. There is no ruler and no physics in it, the answer changes with the room, and it can never be brought down to one person. A calibrated thermometer on one forehead reads 104.1 for that person, who came in alone: a definite fever, with a cause the thermometer does not claim to name. It reads 100.1 as something to ask a doctor about, and 98.6 as ordinary for someone of that age. It also reads a freezer, because the freezing point of water is fixed whatever else is in the room, and the same construction says how far a quantum computer's cooler sits from absolute zero, because the physics behind it is known and the instrument is calibrated to it.

Every lever in this chapter is a handle on one of those fixed points or on the measured middle. A lever that moves the drive moves the FLOOR; a lever that pushes a specimen toward beta = 1/2 runs it at the CEILING, past which the reading is no longer monotone; a lever that changes the balance of restore and loss moves the MIDDLE, which is the only mark that was ever measured. The class era (retired) was the back of a hand across a room; this chapter is the thermometer, and its job is to say what would prove the calibration wrong.

And what the chapter does NOT claim: the gauge never sees an enzyme. It reads informational fidelity - whether the pattern is still held, how far it has drifted, and whether its errors are isolated or run together. Every mechanism named below is a handle pulled in an experiment or an inference drawn afterwards, labelled as one.
_reading_scope: Every lever below is a HANDLE PULLED IN AN EXPERIMENT. The reading is not of the handle: it is informational fidelity, order against disorder in the held pattern, as errors in individual molecules (CANON/foundation.json, entry what_is_read). So no row here may be read as 'the gauge identified which machine failed'. What a lever earns is narrower and stronger: pull this handle and the held error, or the clustering of its errors, must move the derived way - and if it does not, the law is wrong there.
_layer: Every lever is MEDIUM, not core (see the foundation record). The law is substrate-free; a lever is how a handle reaches one of its terms in a cell. So each lever's falsifier must declare its SCOPE: 'law' only where the handle reaches the term with nothing fitted in between, 'medium' where biology sits in the way. Getting the medium wrong says nothing about the law; and a law-scope failure may not be excused as a medium error afterwards.
